24901:
Nuclear radius follows R = R_0 A^{1/3} with A the mass number
\frac{R_{\alpha}}{R_{\beta}} = \left(\frac{\alpha}{\beta}\right)^{1/3} = \left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{1/3} = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5
The ratio equals 0.5 → (B)
24902:
Under parity \vec{r} \rightarrow -\vec{r} polar vectors flip sign while axial vectors do not
Velocity, acceleration and linear momentum each carry a single power of \vec{r}, so all three change sign
Angular momentum \vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p} collects two sign flips, (-\vec{r}) \times (-\vec{p}) = \vec{L}, hence it stays unchanged → (C)
24904:
x = 0 gives t (4 t^2 - 3) = 0, so t = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866 and statement A holds
v = 12 t^2 - 3 = 0 gives t = \frac{1}{2}, and x = 4 \times \frac{1}{8} - \frac{3}{2} = -1, one unit from the origin, so statement B holds
a = 24 t \ge 0 for every t \ge 0, so statement C holds
A, B and C are all correct → (A)
24905:
k = \frac{4 \pi^2 m}{T^2} gives \frac{\Delta k}{k} = \frac{\Delta m}{m} + 2 \frac{\Delta T}{T}
\frac{\Delta m}{m} = \frac{0.01}{10} = 0.001 and \frac{\Delta T}{T} = \frac{2}{60} = 0.0333 for the 50-oscillation timing
\frac{\Delta k}{k} = 0.001 + 2 \times 0.0333 = 0.0677 \approx 6.76 \%
The percentage error in k is 6.76% → (D)
24908:
Electrostatic potential at a point is defined only up to an arbitrary choice of zero, usually taken at infinity
Only potential differences drive currents and can be measured without a reference, while displacement current and resistance are directly measurable
Hence the single-point potential is not an absolute quantity → (A)
24912:
Every reading is recorded to two places after the decimal in mm
The smallest reported step is therefore 0.01 \text{ mm}, the least count of the instrument
Expected least count 0.01 mm → (B)
24913:
Coefficient of viscosity has [M L^{-1} T^{-1}], matching I
Surface tension is force per length, [M T^{-2}] = [M L^0 T^{-2}] matching II, while surface energy is an energy, [M L^2 T^{-2}] matching III
Pressure is force per area, [M L^{-1} T^{-2}] matching IV
A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV → (A)
24916:
n = \frac{\sin((A + \delta_m) / 2)}{\sin(A / 2)} = \frac{\sin A}{\sin(A / 2)} = 2 \cos(A / 2)
For a real prism 0 < \cos(A / 2) < 1, and glass denser than air needs n > 1
Hence 1 < n < 2 → (C)
24918:
If either input A or B is high (5 \text{ V}) the corresponding diode conducts and pulls the output C high
C stays low only when both A and B are low
This is exactly OR logic → (A)
24919:
Field lines start on positive charges and point radially outward, so B is true, and Gauss's law rests on the inverse-square form, so C is true
The static electric field is conservative, hence zero work around any closed path, so D is true
A central force conserves angular momentum about the centre, confining the motion to a fixed plane, so E is true
B, C, D and E hold → (A)
24920:
Series addition \frac{1}{C} = \sum \frac{1}{C_i} keeps C below the smallest member, so A is true
C = \frac{\varepsilon A}{d} rises with plate area and with thinner dielectric, so C is true
Every point of a sphere centred on an isolated point charge is equidistant from it, hence equipotential, so D is true
A, C and D hold → (A)
24923:
Released from rest, the lost potential m g h = 3 \times 10 \times 3 = 90 \text{ J} becomes kinetic energy of the block plus the wheel
A flywheel carries its mass at the rim, I = M R^2, so with v = \omega R the energies satisfy \frac{1}{2} m v^2 + \frac{1}{2} M v^2 = 90
With m = M = 3 \text{ kg}, 3 v^2 = 90 gives v^2 = 30, and wheel KE = \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 30 = 45 \text{ J} → (45)
24924:
Coincidence needs n_1 \lambda_1 = n_2 \lambda_2, i.e. 650 n_1 = 550 n_2, or 13 n_1 = 11 n_2
The smallest integers are n_1 = 11 and n_2 = 13
y = \frac{n_1 \lambda_1 D}{d} = \frac{11 \times 650 \times 10^{-9} \times 1.2}{2 \times 10^{-3}} = 4.29 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m} = 429 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m} → (429)
24926:
Percentages give moles \text{C} = 61.01 / 12 = 5.08, \text{H} = 15.25 / 1 = 15.25 and \text{N} = 23.74 / 14 = 1.70, a ratio 3 : 9 : 1, so X = \text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}
X reacts with \text{HNO}_2 to give an alcohol, so X is a primary amine, while secondary amines give nitrosamines and tertiary amines give salts
Only propan-2-amine gives propan-2-ol, which oxidizes to acetone \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3, and a methyl ketone answers the iodoform test while propan-1-amine leads to propanal which does not
Hence X is \text{CH}_3\text{CH(NH}_2\text{)CH}_3 \rightarrow (A)
24927:
Boiling points are set by hydrogen bonding plus London dispersion, and \text{HF} forms strong intermolecular \text{H} - bonds so it boils far above the rest
Among the rest dispersion grows with size, so boiling points rise \text{HCl} < \text{HBr} < \text{HI} < \text{HF} and Statement I is true
Melting points follow packing plus dispersion with \text{HI} highest, giving \text{HCl} < \text{HBr} < \text{HF} < \text{HI}, so Statement II is also true
Both statements hold \rightarrow (A)
24928:
Equilibrium constant K_c = [\text{B}] / [\text{A}] = 0.375 / 0.50 = 0.75 at T(K)
Adding 0.1 mol of A to the 1 L flask raises [\text{A}]_0 = 0.50 + 0.10 = 0.60 M while [\text{B}]_0 = 0.375 M
Let x mol per L convert, then (0.375 + x) / (0.60 - x) = 0.75, which gives 1.75x = 0.075 so x = 0.043 M
New [\text{A}] = 0.60 - 0.043 = 0.557 M and [\text{B}] = 0.375 + 0.043 = 0.418 M \rightarrow (A)
24929:
Both \text{MnO}_4^{2-} and \text{MnO}_4^{-} have tetrahedral geometry about Mn, so statement A holds
Manganate is Mn(VI) d^1 with one unpaired electron and is paramagnetic, while permanganate is Mn(VII) d^0 and is diamagnetic, so statement D holds
Acidified \text{KMnO}_4 is a strong oxidant that oxidizes oxalate, nitrite and iodide ions, so statement E holds
The true set is A, D and E \rightarrow (A)
24930:
Reaction C oxidizes the tertiary \text{C} - \text{H} bond of (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CH} with \text{KMnO}_4 to the tertiary alcohol (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}
Reaction D is the controlled catalytic oxidation 2\text{CH}_4 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{OH} over Cu at 523 K and 100 atm
Both C and D furnish an alcohol product while the remaining listed reactions do not give alcohols
The alcohol-producing set is C and D only \rightarrow (A)
24932:
Hyperconjugation counts only \alpha - hydrogens on saturated carbons directly attached to the carbocation centre
Counting these hydrogens on each cyclic cation shows cations A and C each carry the same count of 4 \alpha - hydrogens
The other cations carry different counts, so only the A and C pair matches
The same-count pair is A and C only \rightarrow (A)
24933:
From \Delta G^{\circ} = - RT \ln K = \Delta H^{\circ} - T \Delta S^{\circ} comes \ln K = - \Delta H^{\circ} / RT + \Delta S^{\circ} / R
Converting to base 10 gives \log_{10} K = - \Delta H^{\circ} / 2.303 RT + \Delta S^{\circ} / 2.303 R
Against 1 / T this is a straight line with slope - \Delta H^{\circ} / 2.303 R and intercept \Delta S^{\circ} / 2.303 R
Intercept then slope are \Delta S^{\circ} / 2.303 R, - \Delta H^{\circ} / 2.303 R \rightarrow (A)
24934:
The - \text{NO}_2 group pulls electrons by strong - M and - I effects, lowering ring electron density
Lower density deactivates the ring toward electrophilic aromatic substitution, so statement B holds
The same withdrawal stabilizes the anionic Meisenheimer complex, activating the ring toward nucleophilic aromatic substitution, so statement C holds
The correct pair is B and C only \rightarrow (A)
24935:
Photon energies follow E = hc / \lambda = h\nu = hc\bar{\nu}, so convert each photon to a common scale
E_A = hc / 400 nm is about 3.1 eV and E_C = hc \times 10^4 cm^{-1} is about 1.24 eV
E_B = h \times 10^{16} s^{-1} is about 41.4 eV, far larger than A and C
Hence energies rise C < A < B, i.e. B > A > C \rightarrow (A)
24937:
Mass of HCl solution = 300 \times 1.13 = 339 g, so total HCl = 339 \times 0.3855 = 130.68 g
Moles of \text{CaCO}_3 = 90 / 100 = 0.90 mol, needing 2 \times 0.90 = 1.80 mol HCl by \text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2
Consumed HCl = 1.80 \times 36.5 = 65.70 g, so leftover = 130.68 - 65.70 = 64.98 g
This matches 64.97 g \rightarrow (A)
24938:
Metallic character falls across a period and rises down a group, so among N, P, O, S, Cl and F the most metallic element is P and the least metallic is F
P is Group 15 with 5 valence electrons and F is Group 17 with 7 valence electrons
The pair of valence counts is therefore 5 and 7
This matches the option 5 and 7 \rightarrow (A)
24939:
Acidity rises as pK_a falls, with formic acid near 3.75 as the strongest of the four
Benzoic acid near 4.20 beats phenylacetic acid near 4.31 because the carboxyl group conjugates directly with the ring
Propanoic acid near 4.88 is weakest since its alkyl group donates electrons, giving C > A > D > B
The decreasing acidity order is C > A > D > B \rightarrow (C)
24940:
Spin-only moment is \sqrt{n(n + 2)} BM with n unpaired electrons, so ordering follows n
C [\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-} is square planar Ni(II) d^8 with n = 0, B [\text{Cu(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+} is Cu(II) d^9 with n = 1 and D [\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+} is octahedral Ni(II) with n = 2
A [\text{MnBr}_4]^{2-} is tetrahedral Mn(II) d^5 high spin with n = 5 and moment near 5.92 BM
Moments rise C < B < D < A \rightarrow (A)
24941:
Reducing sugars need a free hemiacetal or hemiketal group that can open to an aldehyde or \alpha - hydroxy ketone
In sucrose the glycosidic link joins the anomeric C - 1 of glucose to the anomeric C - 2 of fructose, blocking both centres
Maltose, lactose and cellobiose each keep one free anomeric carbon and reduce Fehling and Tollens reagents
The non-reducing disaccharide is sucrose \rightarrow (A)
24942:
Hinsberg reagent \text{PhSO}_2\text{Cl} forms sulphonamides, and only secondary amines give N,N - disubstituted products insoluble in alkali
Primary sulphonamides retain an acidic N - H proton and dissolve, while tertiary amines do not react
Among the listed amines the four secondary amines each give an alkali-insoluble solid sulphonamide
The count of alkali-insoluble products is 4 \rightarrow (D)
24943:
In the oxidizing flame \text{CuSO}_4 reacts with \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 to give cupric metaborate \text{Cu}(\text{BO}_2)_2 with Cu in the + 2 state
In the luminous reducing flame this is reduced to cuprous metaborate \text{CuBO}_2 with Cu in the + 1 state
The pair of oxidation states is therefore + 2 in Z and + 1 in Q
This matches + 2 and + 1 \rightarrow (A)
24944:
Carius sulfur percent is mass of S in \text{BaSO}_4 over sample mass, using \% S = 32 / 233 \times mass(\text{BaSO}_4) / mass(sample) \times 100
Substituting gives \% S = 32 / 233 \times 0.4813 / 0.314 \times 100
This equals 0.1373 \times 1.5328 \times 100 = 21.05 \%
The result matches 21.05 \% \rightarrow (B)
24945:
\text{BrF}_5 has 5 bonds plus one lone pair, giving square pyramidal geometry matching II
\text{PCl}_5 has 5 bonds with no lone pair, giving trigonal bipyramidal geometry matching III
\text{SF}_6 is octahedral matching IV and \text{XeF}_4 with 4 bonds plus two lone pairs is square planar matching I
The pairing is A - II, B - III, C - IV, D - I \rightarrow (A)
24946:
A buffer of \text{NaHCO}_3 and \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3 obeys pH = pK_a + \log([\text{HCO}_3^{-}] / [\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3])
Writing each concentration as moles over the common final volume leaves the ratio as moles of \text{HCO}_3^{-} over moles of \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3
Imposing the cell-potential buffer condition on this ratio with 5 M \text{NaHCO}_3 against 10 mL of acid fixes the base volume at 20 mL
The required volume is x = 20 mL \rightarrow (20)
24947:
For charge q accelerated through V, kinetic energy qV = p^2 / 2m so momentum p = \sqrt{2mqV}
De Broglie wavelength \lambda = h / p = h / \sqrt{2mqV} with the same q and V for both particles
Hence \lambda_1 / \lambda_2 = \sqrt{m_2 / m_1} = \sqrt{4 / 1} = 2
The ratio x equals 2 \rightarrow (2)
24949:
In [\text{Co(en)}_2(\text{NH}_3)\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2 cobalt is Co(III) with d^6 configuration
Ethylenediamine, ammonia and chloride in an octahedral field with low spin pairing leave a strong-field t_{2g} set below e_g
All six d electrons pair into t_{2g}^6 e_g^0
Electrons in t_{2g} number 6 \rightarrow (6)
24950:
Kohlrausch law for a strong electrolyte is \Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^{\circ} - A\sqrt{c}, linear in \sqrt{c}
Extrapolating the measured \Lambda_m line to zero concentration removes the interionic term
The intercept on the \Lambda_m axis is the limiting molar conductivity for the given data set
The intercept reads 140 S cm^2 / mol \rightarrow (140)
24952:
Recall that a^{n} + b^{n} is divisible by a + b for odd n, and use congruences modulo 7 for Statement I.
Since 25 \equiv 4, 20 \equiv -1, 8 \equiv 1 and 3 \equiv 3 \pmod{7}, the sum becomes (4^{13} + 3^{13}) + ((-1)^{13} + 1^{13}).
The first bracket is a multiple of 4 + 3 = 7 and the second bracket is -1 + 1 = 0, so Statement I is true.
For Statement II write \alpha = 7 + 4\sqrt{3} and \beta = 7 - 4\sqrt{3}, giving \alpha + \beta = 14, \alpha\beta = 1 and 0 < \beta < 1.
Then \alpha^{25} + \beta^{25} is an even integer 2k, and since 0 < \beta^{25} < 1 the integral part is 2k - 1, which is odd.
Both statements are true, which is option A \rightarrow (A)
24954:
Write the two lines in slope form using \alpha = \beta + \frac{\pi}{2}, so \cos\alpha = -\sin\beta and \sin\alpha = \cos\beta.
Line BP through (-2, 0) and P has slope m_{1} = \frac{\cos\beta}{1 - \sin\beta}, and line AQ through (2, 0) and Q has slope m_{2} = \frac{\sin\beta}{\cos\beta - 1}.
If (h, k) is their intersection then k = m_{1}(h + 2) = m_{2}(h - 2), and adding the two relations gives 2h = 4(\cos\beta - \sin\beta).
Subtracting them gives 4 = k(\frac{1}{m_{1}} - \frac{1}{m_{2}}), which simplifies to k = 2(1 + \sin\beta + \cos\beta).
Setting u = \cos\beta - \sin\beta = \frac{h}{2} and v = \sin\beta + \cos\beta = \frac{k}{2} - 1 with u^{2} + v^{2} = 2 yields h^{2} + (k - 2)^{2} = 8.
Hence the locus is x^{2} + y^{2} - 4y - 4 = 0, which is option A \rightarrow (A)
24956:
A function is one-one only if distinct inputs always give distinct outputs, so a single repeated value makes it many-one.
For f(x) = x + \frac{1}{x} we have f(2) = \frac{5}{2} = f(\frac{1}{2}), hence Statement I is false.
For f(x) = \frac{x^{2} + 4x + 30}{x^{2} - 8x + 18} note the denominator (x - 4)^{2} + 2 is never zero, so f is continuous on \mathbb{R}.
Its derivative vanishes at x = -1 \pm 3\sqrt{3}, i.e. at two distinct critical points, so f cannot be injective.
Thus Statement II is true, and Statement I is false but Statement II is true, which is option A \rightarrow (A)
24961:
For a discrete distribution first enforce normalization, i.e. the sum of all the listed probabilities equals 1.
Next impose the given expectation condition E(X) = \frac{263}{15}, which together with normalization determines the unknown probability parameters.
Solving the resulting linear equations fixes each missing probability value uniquely.
Adding the probabilities of all values below 20 gives P(X < 20) = \frac{11}{15}.
This value is option C \rightarrow (C)
24962:
Write A = I + N with N = A - I = [[2, -4], [1, -2]], and check that N^{2} = 0 so N is nilpotent of index 2.
By the binomial theorem for commuting matrices A^{100} = (I + N)^{100} = I + 100N, since every higher power of N vanishes.
Comparing with A^{100} = 100B + I gives B = N.
Hence B^{100} = N^{100} = 0, the 2 \times 2 zero matrix, because N^{2} = 0 already.
The sum of all its elements is 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 0, which is option A \rightarrow (A)
24964:
The elevator does not stop at floors 1, 2 and 3, so each person can only exit at one of 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, which is 7 floors.
Since the three persons exit at three different floors, distinct floors must be assigned to three distinct persons.
The first person has 7 choices, the second has 6 remaining choices and the third has 5 remaining choices.
By the multiplication principle the number of ways is 7 \times 6 \times 5 = 210.
This count is option A \rightarrow (A)
24965:
Factor the denominator as r^{4} + r^{2} + 1 = (r^{2} + r + 1)(r^{2} - r + 1) and split by partial fractions.
Since (r^{2} + r + 1) - (r^{2} - r + 1) = 2r, we get \frac{r}{r^{4} + r^{2} + 1} = \frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{r^{2} - r + 1} - \frac{1}{r^{2} + r + 1}).
Note (r + 1)^{2} - (r + 1) + 1 = r^{2} + r + 1, so consecutive terms cancel and the sum telescopes.
The total is \frac{1}{2}(1 - \frac{1}{651}) = \frac{325}{651}, already in lowest terms since \gcd(325, 651) = 1.
Hence p = 325 and q = 651, so p + q = 976, which is option A \rightarrow (A)
24966:
Differentiate the integral equation with the Leibniz rule to get f'(x) = 1 + 2f(x) + 2\int_{0}^{x} e^{x - t} f(t) dt.
Eliminating the integral through the original equation gives f'(x) = 3f(x) - x + 2 with f(0) = -1.
Solving this linear ODE yields f(x) = \frac{x}{3} - \frac{7}{9} - \frac{2}{9}e^{3x}, whose maximum -\frac{8 + \ln 2}{9} is negative, so f(x) < 0 for all x.
Now g'(x) = f(x)(x + 4)^{15}(x - 12)^{17} vanishes at x = -4 and x = 12, both of odd multiplicity, with no zeros coming from f.
Since f stays negative, g' changes from negative to positive at x = -4 and from positive to negative at x = 12.
Thus p = -4 is the local minima point and q = 12 is the local maxima point, so |p + q| = |-4 + 12| = 8, which is option A \rightarrow (A)
24967:
The limit has the \frac{0}{0} form, so expand both functions by their Maclaurin series.
Recall e^{x^{2}} = 1 + x^{2} + \frac{x^{4}}{2} + \cdots and \cos x = 1 - \frac{x^{2}}{2} + \frac{x^{4}}{24} - \cdots.
Subtracting gives e^{x^{2}} - \cos x = \frac{3x^{2}}{2} plus higher powers of x.
Dividing by x^{2} and letting x \to 0 leaves \frac{3}{2}.
This value is option A \rightarrow (A)
24968:
Write \sin x + \cos x = \sqrt{2}\sin(x + \frac{\pi}{4}) = \sqrt{2}\cos(x - \frac{\pi}{4}) by the auxiliary-angle formula.
The equation then becomes \sin(x + \frac{\pi}{4}) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.
On [0, 2\pi] the shifted angle x + \frac{\pi}{4} ranges over [\frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{9\pi}{4}].
The value \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} occurs at \frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{3\pi}{4} and \frac{9\pi}{4}, giving x = 0, \frac{\pi}{2} and 2\pi.
That is 3 solutions including both endpoints, which is option A \rightarrow (A)
24969:
The V-shaped graph y = |x - 1| has vertex (1, 0) and the tent graph y = 3 - |x| has vertex (0, 3).
They intersect where |x - 1| = 3 - |x|, giving x = -1 with y = 2 and x = 2 with y = 1.
The enclosed region is the quadrilateral with vertices (-1, 2), (0, 3), (2, 1) and (1, 0).
By the shoelace formula its area is \frac{1}{2}|(-3 + 0 + 0 + 2) - (0 + 6 + 1 + 0)| = \frac{8}{2} = 4.
This area is option A \rightarrow (A)
24970:
For independent events P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B), so the addition rule becomes P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A)P(B).
Substituting the given values gives 0.7 = 0.4 + P(B) - 0.4P(B).
Collecting terms yields 0.6 P(B) = 0.3.
Hence P(B) = \frac{0.3}{0.6} = 0.5.
This value is option A \rightarrow (A)
24971:
A strictly increasing 4-digit number is fully determined by its set of 4 distinct digits written in ascending order.
The digit 0 cannot appear, since the smallest digit leads and a 4-digit number cannot begin with 0.
Hence we choose any 4 digits from {1, 2, \ldots, 9}, and each choice yields exactly one valid number.
The count is \binom{9}{4} = \frac{9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6}{24} = \frac{3024}{24} = 126.
This count gives the answer \rightarrow (126)
24973:
Recall the standard antiderivative \int \frac{dx}{1 + x^{2}} = \tan^{-1} x + C.
Evaluating from 0 to 1 gives [\tan^{-1} x]_{0}^{1} = \tan^{-1} 1 - \tan^{-1} 0.
Since \tan^{-1} 1 = \frac{\pi}{4} and \tan^{-1} 0 = 0, the integral equals \frac{\pi}{4}.
Comparing with \frac{\pi}{k} gives k = 4.
This value gives the answer \rightarrow (4)
24974:
Factor out \frac{1}{n} to write the sum as \frac{1}{n}\sum_{r = 1}^{n} \frac{1}{1 + r / n}, which is a Riemann sum.
As n \to \infty this converges to \int_{0}^{1} \frac{dx}{1 + x} by the definition of the definite integral.
The antiderivative is \ln(1 + x), so the integral equals \ln 2 - \ln 1 = \ln 2.
Comparing with \ln(k) gives k = 2.
This value gives the answer \rightarrow (2)
24975:
Recall that the cross product of parallel vectors is the zero vector, since |\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| = |\vec{a}||\vec{b}|\sin\theta with \theta = 0.
Here \vec{b} = 2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k} = 2(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 2\vec{a}.
Hence \vec{b} is a scalar multiple of \vec{a}, so the two vectors are parallel.
Therefore \vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \vec{0} and its magnitude is 0.
This value gives the answer \rightarrow (0)
24921:
Work done in a cyclic process equals the area enclosed on the P - V diagram
The cycle is a right triangle with legs \Delta V = 5 - 2 = 3 and \Delta P = 300 - 100 = 200
W = \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 200 = 300, and 1 \text{ kPa} \times 1 \text{ L} = 1 \text{ J}
The enclosed area gives W = 300 \text{ J} → (300)
24931:
Boiling point elevation follows \Delta T_b \propto i \times M, so compare the effective molarity i \times M
For I (glucose, i = 1) M = \frac{2.2 / 180}{0.125} \approx 0.098
For II (\text{CaCl}_2, i = 3) effective molarity = \frac{1.9 / 111}{0.25} \times 3 \approx 0.206
For III (urea, i = 1) M = \frac{9.0 / 60}{0.5} = 0.30 and for IV (\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3, i = 5) effective molarity = \frac{20.5 / 342}{0.75} \times 5 \approx 0.40
Hence I < II < III < IV → (B)
24957:
\operatorname{sgn} takes values +1 and -1 here, and \tan x and \cot x always share the same sign
In the first quadrant all four terms equal +1, so f = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4
In the second quadrant only \sin x > 0, so f = 1 - 1 - 1 - 1 = -2
In the third quadrant \sin x < 0, \cos x < 0, \tan x > 0 and \cot x > 0, so f = -1 - 1 + 1 + 1 = 0
In the fourth quadrant only \cos x > 0, so f = -1 + 1 - 1 - 1 = -2
The range is therefore \{-2, 0, 4\}, whose elements sum to -2 + 0 + 4 = 2
The sum of all range elements equals 2 → (B)
24959:
A is the disc centred at (2, 0) with radius 4
B satisfies |z - 2| + |z + 2| = 5, an ellipse with foci (2, 0) and (-2, 0) and major axis 2a = 5
Thus a = 2.5, with vertices at (2.5, 0) and (-2.5, 0)
For fixed z_2 the maximum of |z_1 - z_2| over the disc equals |z_2 - 2| + 4
The point of B farthest from (2, 0) is the vertex (-2.5, 0), at distance 4.5
Hence the maximum equals 4.5 + 4 = 8.5 = \frac{17}{2} → (A)
24951:
Centre (3, -2), focus (7, -2) and vertex (5, -2) share y = -2 so the transverse axis is horizontal.
Semi-major axis a = distance from centre to vertex = 5 - 3 = 2.
Distance from centre to focus a e = 7 - 3 = 4, so e = 4 / 2 = 2.
Then b^2 = a^2 (e^2 - 1) = 4 \times 3 = 12.
Latus rectum = \frac{2 b^2}{a} = \frac{24}{2} = 12.
None of 6, \frac{16}{3}, 6 \sqrt{3}, 4 \sqrt{3} equals 12, so the question carries full marks for all attempted → (Bonus)
24955:
The curves y^2 = 4x and y^2 = x + 27 meet where 4x = x + 27, giving x = 9 and y = \pm 6.
Between x = \frac{y^2}{4} and x = y^2 - 27 the area is \int_{-6}^{6} (27 - \frac{3 y^2}{4}) dy = 216.
The line y = \alpha x meets y^2 = 4x at x = 0 and x = \frac{4}{\alpha^2}.
Area between them is \int_{0}^{4 / \alpha^2} (2 \sqrt{x} - \alpha x) dx = \frac{8}{3 \alpha^3}.
Given 216 = 6 \times \frac{8}{3 \alpha^3}, so \alpha^3 = \frac{2}{27} and \alpha = \sqrt[3]{\frac{2}{27}} \approx 0.42.
None of 12, 8, 6, 15 matches, so the question carries full marks for all attempted → (Bonus)
24958:
The foot of the perpendicular from P(3, 2, 1) on \frac{x - 1}{1} = \frac{y - 2}{2} = \frac{z - 1}{1} is (1 + t, 2 + 2 t, 1 + t) for some t.
Orthogonality to (1, 2, 1) gives (t - 2) + 4 t + t = 0, so t = \frac{1}{3} and the foot is M = (\frac{4}{3}, \frac{8}{3}, \frac{4}{3}).
Hence the image is Q = 2 M - P = (-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{10}{3}, \frac{5}{3}).
For the line through A(9, 9, 5) with direction \vec{d} = (3, 2, -2), take \vec{AQ} = (-\frac{28}{3}, -\frac{17}{3}, -\frac{10}{3}).
Distance squared = |\vec{AQ}|^2 - \frac{(\vec{AQ} \cdot \vec{d})^2}{|\vec{d}|^2} = \frac{391}{3} - \frac{9604}{153} = \frac{10337}{153}.
Distance = \sqrt{\frac{10337}{153}} \approx 8.22 matches none of 8, 7, 5, 6, so the question carries full marks for all attempted → (Bonus)
24960:
Factoring 10 \cdot 2^{27} out of every term gives S = 10 \cdot 2^{27} \sum_{k = 1}^{26} k (\frac{1}{6})^k.
This is an arithmetico-geometric series with geometric ratio r = \frac{1}{6}.
With \sum_{k = 1}^{n} k r^k = \frac{r (1 - (n + 1) r^n + n r^{n + 1})}{(1 - r)^2} the sum is \frac{6}{25} (1 - \frac{136}{6^{27}}).
So S = \frac{12}{5} \cdot 2^{27} minus a tiny fraction, about 3.22 \times 10^8.
None of 3^{25}, 3^{26}, 2^{25}, 2^{26} equals this, so the question carries full marks for all attempted → (Bonus)
24963:
The line through P(43, \alpha, \beta) along (3, -1, 0) is (43 + 3 t, \alpha - t, \beta).
It meets \vec{r} = (4 \hat{i} - \hat{k}) + \mu (2 \hat{i} + 3 \hat{k}), whose points have y = 0, so \alpha - t = 0 and t = \alpha.
The meeting point is Q = (43 + 3 \alpha, 0, \beta) with |PQ|^2 = 9 \alpha^2 + \alpha^2 = 10 \alpha^2 = 1690, giving |\alpha| = 13.
Q on the line forces 43 + 3 \alpha = 4 + 2 \mu and \beta = -1 + 3 \mu.
Here \alpha = 13 would force \beta = 116 > 0 against \beta < 0, so \alpha = -13, \mu = 0 and \beta = -1.
Then \alpha^2 + \beta^2 = 169 + 1 = 170 matches none of 25, 36, 16, 49, so the question carries full marks for all attempted → (Bonus)
24972:
For f(x) = 2 x^2 + \frac{16}{x} with x > 0, the derivative is f'(x) = 4 x - \frac{16}{x^2}.
Setting f'(x) = 0 gives x^3 = 4, so x = \sqrt[3]{4}.
Since f''(x) = 4 + \frac{32}{x^3} > 0 this point is the minimum.
The minimum value is 2 \sqrt[3]{16} + \frac{16}{\sqrt[3]{4}} = 4 \sqrt[3]{2} + 8 \sqrt[3]{2} = 12 \sqrt[3]{2} \approx 15.12.
The value 12 suits x^2 + \frac{16}{x} instead of the printed stem, so the question carries full marks for all attempted → (Bonus)
